title: Canary stripping deletes specification content through later HTML comments
reasoning: The greedy [\s\S]+ matches through the last matching comment terminator in the specification. When a leading canary is followed by specification text and another HTML comment, stripping removes the intervening requirements as well. render_prompt applies this transformation automatically, so the agent receives an incomplete specification.
reproduction:
strip_canary_string('<!-- CANARY -->
Required behavior
<!-- note -->
Remaining text') returns 'Remaining text', losing 'Required behavior'.
recommendation: Bound matching to the first closing comment delimiter, preserving all subsequent specification content.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests cover a leading canary and a non-leading comment separately, but never combine them in one specification.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand canary stripping scenarios to include leading single-line and multiline canaries followed by requirements and additional HTML comments; assert the entire suffix is preserved.

commands:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from slop_code.common.render import strip_canary_string, render_prompt
suffix = 'Required behavior\n<!-- note -->\nRemaining text'
for prefix in ('<!-- CANARY -->\n', '<!-- CANARY\nTRACKING -->\n'):
    text = prefix + suffix
    assert strip_canary_string(text) == suffix
    assert render_prompt(text, {}, '{{ spec }}', 'main.py', 'python main.py') == suffix
print('Original reproduction and multiline variant preserve the complete suffix through stripping and prompt rendering.')
PY
